MGT 409 · AI Foundations for Managers · Final project

PhysioTeam

A team of six AI agents that runs the back office of a solo physical therapy clinic on WhatsApp, and frees about one billable hour a day of the therapist's time.
AuthorJose Tronco · jesus.troncovalencia@yale.edu GitHub repohttps://github.com/JoseTronco98/physioteam · public repo · clone: git clone https://github.com/JoseTronco98/physioteam Run it (~5 min)pip install -r requirements.txt → put PORTKEY_API_KEY in .env → python run.py → http://localhost:8000. Python only; the React build is committed. Full steps: Appendix A. Live appNot hosted permanently (the course key would be public). A Render blueprint (render.yaml) deploys it in one step. What it doesPatients write on WhatsApp; six AI agents book, apply the clinic's policies, chase payments, draft every clinical form and doctor report, and report results. The therapist only approves. Demo videoSubmitted with this report (5 minutes), recorded on the tester's own computer: introductions, the physical therapist who tested PhysioTeam on the three pain points and the ~2 hours a day they take, Demo 1 (booking) run by the tester, and the tester's verdict. Demos 2 and 3 are traced step by step in Exhibits 6-7.

Executive summary

  1. The answer: PhysioTeam frees about one billable hour a day of the therapist's time: about 22 more consultations and about MXN 8,800 a month in impact, for about MXN 183 a month to run (case study: a solo physical therapy clinic in Mexico; initial estimate, n = 1; section 6).
  2. The problem. A solo physical therapist is also the clinic's receptionist, biller and secretary: about 130 minutes a day of booking, reports and payments in the case-study clinic, much of it unpaid time outside sessions.
  3. What PhysioTeam is. Six AI agents with 58 tools answer patients on WhatsApp, book and rebook, apply the cancellation policy, chase payments, and draft every clinical form and doctor report on the clinic's own templates. Competitors cover one or two of these jobs.
  4. The therapist stays in charge. Every booking, charge, document and doctor message waits as an approval card, and code, not the AI, carries it out; all 9 risks in the register (Exhibit 14) are stopped by a defense that passed its test.
  5. The drafts can be trusted as first drafts. On 30 therapist notes the drafting agent filled 93% of the evaluation form and 94% of session notes; 96% of the numbers it wrote appear in the notes, and the rest are flagged.
  6. It is cheap to run. One clinic costs about MXN 183 a month; AI is about 1% of it, WhatsApp fees and hosting the rest (Exhibit 12).

1 · Solo physical therapists in Mexico lose a working day a week to WhatsApp and paperwork, and empty slots to late cancellations

Who has the problem. Most physical therapists in Mexico practice alone or in pairs. The case-study clinic is that kind of practice: one treatment room, about 25 active patients, three sessions a week each. Everything runs through the therapist's personal WhatsApp, the channel Mexico already uses with its health providers: about 78 million users, roughly 60% of the population (Asociación de Internet MX via DPL News).

How it is handled today. Between patients and at night the therapist answers by hand: prices and therapy differences, the address, "can I come Thursday?", the reminder and its "C to confirm", cancellations two hours before a session, "how much do I owe?", receipts for insurance, invoices through an accountant, a gym video with "can I do this?", a daughter booking both parents. After sessions come the forms: a seven-section paper evaluation, a SOAP note per session (the standard session note: subjective, objective, assessment, plan), treatment plans, and progress reports when a referring doctor asks. I read three real (anonymised) patient chats and the clinic's blank paper templates to build this list; none of that data is in the app or the repo.

Exhibit 1Where a solo therapist's admin week goes: about 13 hours, most of it outside clinic hours
Note: volumes measured in PhysioTeam's simulated clinic week (27 patients, 140 inbound WhatsApp messages, 40 sessions); minutes per task assumed (evaluation 20, session note 5, treatment plan 10, doctor report 15, WhatsApp message 2, reminder 0.5). The case-study clinic spends about 130 minutes a day (section 6). Source: PhysioTeam simulation, Oct 2026; author's analysis.

What it costs.

  • Time: about 130 minutes a day in the case-study clinic, including an hour of reports before opening (13 hours a week in the author's model): about a full clinic day a week, unpaid.
  • Money: each empty hour is MXN 400-600 lost. The 24-hour cancellation charge is awkward to apply by hand, so it is often waived, and a freed slot is rarely refilled because nobody has time to text the waitlist.
  • Patients: about 70% of physical therapy patients don't finish their plan of care (WebPT); a 2021 PLOS ONE cohort of about 445,000 patients found 73% missed at least one visit (Bhavsar et al.). Reminders, quick answers and follow-up are what keep them coming.
Why it matters. A receptionist costs more than the hours it would free are worth to a one-room practice, so the admin falls on the therapist: either the therapist's evenings or the patients pay for it.

What is genuinely new

  • One team for the whole loop. A patient's first WhatsApp, the booking, the late cancellation and its fee, the waitlist refill, the evaluation, every SOAP note, the plan, the doctor's report and the week's results are handled by six cooperating agents that pass work to each other.
  • Built from a real clinic. The clinic's evaluation and SOAP forms (same sections, same order), prices, policy and WhatsApp patterns. Output files follow the clinic's naming rule (yymmdd_PatientName_Type).
  • Control by construction. Approval cards are carried out by code, never by the AI; routine clinical questions are batched for the next session instead of interrupting the therapist.
Honest comparison. Doctoralia has a patient marketplace and Jane a certified medical record system; PhysioTeam has neither, and it is not yet connected to a real WhatsApp number (section 7). What it shows is that one small agent team can do the work those tools leave to the therapist, for cents a month.

Exhibit 4Each agent has a narrow job: 58 tools in total, most of them plain code the agents call
AgentRoleToolsRepresentative tools
Operations Partner (lead)Chief of staff: agenda, policy, money, patient logistics21get_agenda, move / book / cancel_appointment, block_time, offer_slot_to_waitlist, book_plan_sessions, agenda_outlook, patient_feedback, answer_patient_question
Health Advisor (lead)Clinical co-pilot; the referring doctors' contact16complete_evaluation, update_evaluation, write_soap_note, propose_treatment_plan, progress_data, draft_progress_report, reply_to_doctor, draft_discharge_summary, read_study
Patient SuccessThe clinic's assistant on WhatsApp; always says it is an AI14clinic_info, find_slots, request_booking, join_waitlist, answer_slot_offer, cancel_or_reschedule, save_intake, my_balance, record_payment_proof, escalate_to_therapist

Imaging ReaderReads study photos and PDFs (vision) after the hidden-text scan-Structured output: ImagingSummary

How they are organised. Keyword rules (with an AI fallback) send each message from the therapist to the right lead. Leads call specialists like tools (functions an agent can use, such as find_slots) and may pass a request to the other lead once (a guard blocks a second hand-off). Patient messages pass the safety layer and go to Patient Success, which can only read the contact's own records and family (enforced in code). Each run is limited to 10 AI calls and 12 tool calls, metered and written to an audit trail. Model: all agents use gpt-6-luna, the course model: cheap ($0.10 per million input tokens, the units of text the AI is billed for), fast and reliable at calling tools and filling forms, which is most of the work. What must never be wrong (prices, policy, approvals, arithmetic) is code, not AI.

Exhibits 5-7 replay exactly those demos with the same scripted patient lines and live agents, and record every step: who acted, what each agent did and which tools it called, the approval cards, the tokens and the cost. What I did to cut cost, and the evidence it did not hurt quality

  • Code wherever a rule is enough. Reminders, "C to confirm", accepted waitlist offers, the 1-5 feedback round, the policy, prices and arithmetic run at zero tokens: 176 of 191 outgoing patient messages (92%) in the measured week. 16 of the 51 story steps cost nothing.
  • Prompt caching. Long stable instructions first, so automatic caching serves 83% of input at a tenth of the price. The A/B (Exhibit 13) produced identical work: 2 bookings, 4 documents, 1 safety block, 0 errors in both arms.
  • Small model, tight loops. One model for all agents, keyword rules before any AI routing, history trimmed to 24 messages, at most 10 requests and 12 tool calls per run, one hand-off per request.
  • Quality check. With these settings the scribe still fills 93% of the evaluation form and keeps 96% of numbers grounded (Exhibit 15); all 51 story steps pass end to end for $0.028.

6 · Case study, initial estimate: PhysioTeam frees about one billable hour a day of the therapist's time, about MXN 8,800 a month in impact

Case study method. Subject: one solo physical therapy clinic in Mexico (one treatment room, ~25 active patients, 3 sessions a week each). Source: physical therapist Juliana del Bosque, who ran the three demos on a recorded call on 2026-10-26 and gave estimates of the clinic's operation. Juliana del Bosque consented to be named as the source of this case study and to appear in the demo video. Clinic hours: today 9:00-18:00 (9 billable hours), with reports written 8:00-9:00, unpaid, before opening; with PhysioTeam 8:00-18:00 (10 billable hours). Data: her best estimates (before), the author's assumptions (after), demand for the extra hour assumed. Scope: initial estimate, n = 1; the four-week pilot will measure it by stopwatch (section 7).

In the case-study clinic, the therapist spends about an hour before opening finishing the previous day's reports, about 5 minutes of every working hour on WhatsApp booking, and about 30 minutes after closing on collections and debts. With PhysioTeam those 130 minutes become about 19 of review and approval cards (Exhibit 18). That frees about one billable hour a day: one more consultation a day, about 22 a month, about MXN 8,800 a month in impact, against about MXN 183 of running cost (Exhibit 19).

Reach (illustrative): at least 3,360 physical therapists and related professionals work in Mexico (DataMéxico, physical therapists, audiologists and speech therapists employed, Q1 2026; a lower bound: the survey groups three professions and misses many self-employed therapists); at 41 h a month each, about 136,752 hours a month. Clinic hours: the case-study clinic works 9:00-18:00; PhysioTeam extends its billable day to 8:00-18:00. The app's simulated clinic uses different hours (11:00-20:00).
  • Cross-check: in the simulated clinic week the same per-task minutes give 13 hours of weekly admin before and 2.4 after: 10 hours freed a week, against 9 in the case study.
  • Money: refilled cancellations recovered MXN 1,200 in one week (two slots offered, accepted and booked within a minute, one tap each). Over a month that is about MXN 5,160, on top of the extra consultations. In the simulated week, 176 of 191 outgoing patient messages (92%) went out from code at zero tokens, and no patient message needed the therapist urgently.
  • Patients: every session ends with a 1-5 rating and a "why" stored in the patient's feedback file (40 ratings in the week, average 4.6); low ratings reach the therapist the same day. Reminders and fast answers are the levers against the ~70% plan drop-out the industry reports.

7 · Three things stand between this prototype and a real clinic: the WhatsApp number, health-data rules, and a month of measured use

Exhibit 20What does not work yet, and what I would build next
Limit todayWhy it mattersNext step
Not on a real WhatsApp number. The Cloud API channel is built and tested locally (webhook, signature check, retries, allowlist, Mexican number format); connecting needs a Meta business account.Patients still write to the demo, not to the clinic's phoneRegister the clinic number on the WhatsApp Cloud API; its per-message fees are already in the running cost (Exhibit 12)
The impact is an initial estimate from one case-study clinic (n = 1): the source's best estimates, assumed review times, and demand assumed to fill the extra hour.One clinic may not represent othersFour-week pilot in the case-study clinic: stopwatch 10 evaluations and the daily report work, count the extra consultations booked in the freed hour; then two or three more solo practices
Fictional data. Patients, doctors and notes are written to the clinic's forms by the course model; small inconsistencies exist.Real notes are messierPilot on the therapist's real (consented) notes for a month
Text only. Voice notes and WhatsApp photos are not read yet (uploads are).Therapists dictateVoice-note dictation into session notes
No calendar or accounting integration (agenda and ledger live in the app; a calendar export exists).Double entryGoogle Calendar and Mexican e-invoicing (CFDI)
Health-data rules. Mexico's data-protection law needs a privacy notice, consent and a provider agreement for the model.Required before real patientsConsent flow in the first WhatsApp message; data-processing agreement
Answers in English only in this build (a project decision).The clinic's patients write SpanishRe-enable the Spanish paths already in the code
Next 90 days: (1) connect the clinic's number and run a four-week pilot measuring hours saved by stopwatch, extra consultations booked in the freed hour, refilled slots and plan completion against the four weeks before; (2) add standard outcome questionnaires (LEFS for the leg, Oswestry for the back) scored in code to the progress reports; (3) offer it to two more solo practices at a price point under MXN 500 a month.

A · Every number, screenshot and document in this report can be regenerated from the repo with the commands below

A1 · Run the app (about 5 minutes; a fresh install took ~4 min)

git clone https://github.com/JoseTronco98/physioteam
cd physioteam
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate          # macOS/Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env          # add PORTKEY_API_KEY=...
python run.py                   # http://localhost:8000

Then: Therapist → Stories (5 stories, one click per step) or Free play; Patient to chat as a persona. Each visitor gets a private sandbox; Reset starts over.

A4 · Data provenance

  • All patients, doctors, chats and notes are fictional, written to the real clinic's templates. No real patient data is in the repo or was sent to the model.
  • backend/clinical_history.json (15 patients' evaluations, plans, one SOAP per past session) from tools/make_history.py; 30 sample notes in backend/demo_files/notes/ from tools/make_notes.py.
  • Prices, policy and forms: backend/store.py. Model outputs vary run to run: re-runs give the same order of magnitude, not identical decimals.
